brief: Morgan Stanley's weekly hedge fund positioning note (data through Oct 1, 2026) says HFs stayed reluctant to add risk amid a macro and geopolitical overhang, producing a quiet week on volumes and themes. US long/short net leverage held flat at 52% (56th percentile since 2010) while gross leverage ticked up to 207% (91st percentile since 2010), as funds were small net sellers of global equities across North America, Europe and APAC. Energy selling continued (sold 13 of the last 15 sessions after July-August buying), concentrated in Crude Levered names even as E&P exposure sits near 12-month lows. Health Care was sold, driven by MedTech and Life Science Tools. In TMT, funds bought Infrastructure Software and Cybersecurity but were net sellers of the Agentic AI and AI Tech Beneficiaries baskets. EU equity exposure stayed near record lows: funds added shorts rather than unwinding longs, and EU-based funds are now most overweight US versus EU equities in five years, though they have not yet turned buyers of EU names. September was a weak month globally (-60bps, +7% YTD), with Americas L/S funds -1.6% in September but +8.4% YTD versus the S&P 500's +12.7%.
